title: Inference Gap Atlas: Field Probe & Fallback Readiness
creator: Priya Nair
description: Objective: Build an "Inference Gap Atlas" — a prioritized, evidence-backed map of where customer workloads are most sensitive to model availability, latency, and pricing trade-offs, and produce a field-ready set of fallback readiness triggers and procurement policy recommendations. Background: Customers increasingly rely on predictable latency and cost. Existing competitive intelligence catalogs model capabilities but do not connect directly to observed customer workload sensitivity. This ticket combines competitive analysis, market research interviews, and synthetic field probes to quantify where we should harden fallbacks (model variants, routing, reserved capacity) versus where we can optimize for cost (quantizations, batching). Scope: - Run 3 enterprise-grade field probes with customers and internal customers (SRE, solution engineers) to capture real latency and quality tolerance thresholds. - Produce a ranked atlas (region x workload archetype) of fallback urgency. - Deliver procurement triggers (when to reserve Dedicated capacity vs allow hosted fallback) and console UX spec for exposing fallback policies to customers.
acceptance_criteria: Atlas: A spreadsheet + dashboard with region x workload archetype rows and scores for latency sensitivity, quality sensitivity, and procurement urgency.
Field probes: Completed interviews + synthetic workload runs for at least 3 customers representing different segments (SaaS PLG, enterprise search, regulated fintech).
Fallback policy playbook: Concrete rules (with thresholds) that map observed signals to actions (canary, fallback-to-quantized-model, reserve-burst-request).
Procurement triggers: Recommended thresholds for Dedicated/Private offerings tied to business signals (monthly qps, 99p latency, quality degradation).
Roadmap: Prioritized list of engineering work and console features with estimates to enable recommended policies.
tasks: Draft hypothesis bank linking competitor availability patterns to customer pain (PM).
Define workload archetypes and synthetic workloads (ENG + PM).
Schedule and run 3 customer field probes; capture telemetry and qualitative feedback (Solutions Eng).
Run synthetic A/B probes against hosted variants and quantized variants; record 50k generated tokens per archetype (ENG).
Analyze output quality tradeoffs using eval prompt sets and automated metrics (Research + PM).
Produce procurement trigger matrix and draft console UX copy for fallback controls (PM + Design).
Review with Legal for any procurement/contract implications (Legal).
Present findings to Leadership and Sales with recommended near-term commitments.
metrics: Customer-reported tolerance: % of customers willing to accept X ms latency increase for Y% cost reduction
Quality delta: BLEU/ROUGE-like proxy or task-specific success rate delta between baseline and fallback models
Latency SLO impact: change in 99th percentile latency when fallback engaged
Estimated unit-cost delta: $/1k tokens change when fallback policies applied
Procurement trigger precision: % of triggers that correctly predict >10% sustained qps growth within 30 days
